Growth and final
preparation
for division

The cell cycle consists of 4 stages. In interphase, which includes its own stages G1, S and G2, the cell prepares for division. In the mitotic stage, nuclear division and cytokinesis (division of the cytoplasm) take place.

Six-hooked

(oncosphere)

Eggs mature in the soil. When an infective egg enters the body, its shell dissolves under the action of the digestive juices, a larva hatches and passes through the stage known as Ascaris larval migration (intestine – venous blood – liver – heart – lungs – alveoli – bronchi – trachea – pharynx – intestine).
